@ashutosh-agrawal Thanks for fixing the deterministic sync-barrier abort. I found one blocking lifecycle issue in the current approach.

`DHCPMgr` remains stack-local in these tests, while `initialize_config_listener()` detaches a thread and `stop_db_updates()` only flips the stop flag. The listener can remain blocked in the 1000 ms `select()` timeout, but the tests wait only 100 ms before the `DHCPMgr` object and test-local global `write()` expectation are destroyed. The next test then calls `InitConfigPipeForTest()`, closing and reusing the global pipe descriptors while the previous listener may still be alive.

That leaves concrete race paths where the old listener accesses the destroyed `DHCPMgr`, invokes the global mock after teardown, or writes to a recycled descriptor—potentially producing another mid-suite abort/terminate or cross-test corruption.

Could you make `DHCPMgr` own the listener thread and join it before destruction and before resetting `config_pipe`? A deterministic completion handshake would also work; another fixed sleep would remain fragile.

Non-blocking cleanup: the helper's `ASSERT_EQ(pipe(...), 0)` only returns from the helper, allowing the test body to continue, and the `fcntl()` result is unchecked. Once #135/#138 are stable, the Makefile's `|| true` should also be removed so CI protects against future aborted or failing test runs.

@StormLiangMS Thanks for the review — addressed the blocking lifecycle issue and the non-blocking InitConfigPipeForTest cleanup.

**Blocking**: listener thread lifecycle 

DHCPMgr now owns a joinable config_listener_thread_ instead of detaching.
stop_db_updates() sets stop_thread and joins the listener if joinable.
initialize_config_listener() calls stop_db_updates() first before starting a new thread.
~DHCPMgr() calls stop_db_updates(), so the listener is joined before the object is destroyed and before the next test's InitConfigPipeForTest() recycles config_pipe.

**Non-blocking**: InitConfigPipeForTest() hardening

Returns bool; checks close/pipe/fcntl with strerror(errno) diagnostics.
Call sites use ASSERT_TRUE(InitConfigPipeForTest()) so setup failure stops the test at the call site.

**Deferred**: Makefile || true

Agreed — will remove once #138 lands and the UT suite is 46/46 passing locally. Without #138, 44/46 tests are passing with this PR.

@ashutosh-agrawal Why duplicate the short-header check in `from_client()` and `to_client()` when `pkt_in_callback()` is their only production caller and already rejects truncated DHCP layers?

@ashutosh-agrawal The production receive buffer is 9,200 bytes. What current path passes `send_udp()` a writable buffer smaller than 300 bytes? Is the padding overflow reachable today, or is this defensive API hardening?
This implementation is mechanically safe, but unnecessary if every current caller has at least 300 writable bytes. Please identify a reachable smaller-buffer path or drop the extra copy/helper.
Same concern for `to_client()`: its only production caller already validates the DHCP header length. Please remove this duplicate guard unless another production call path requires it.
Since this PR already edits the adjacent Doxygen, please also update the `send_udp()` signature to use `in_addr src_ip` and include the `pad` argument.
/azp run

Re [the duplicate `from_client()` guard](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcp-relay/pull/133#issuecomment-5506580759): addressed in a665d46c4. I removed the inner guard and kept the single validation in `pkt_in_callback()` before any DHCP header access.

Re [the 9,200-byte receive-buffer question](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcp-relay/pull/133#issuecomment-5507280728): Good question. The 9,200-byte array is only the buffer used by `recvmsg()`; it is not necessarily the storage that reaches `send_udp()`. When relay options are added, PcapPlusPlus may grow the packet through `Packet::extendLayer()`, which can reallocate the `RawPacket` storage and update the DHCP-layer pointer. That allocation is sized from the captured packet, so it can have less than 300 writable bytes from the DHCP header even though the original receive array was 9,200 bytes. That is the path the local padding buffer protects. The callback check also rejects a truncated DHCP layer before any header access.

Re [the extra copy/helper question](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcp-relay/pull/133#issuecomment-5507460930): You are right that the copy would be unnecessary if `send_udp()` always received a pointer into the 9,200-byte array. The detail is that PcapPlusPlus can replace that storage while extending the parsed packet, so the DHCP pointer can refer to a smaller reallocated buffer. Since `send_udp()` receives the payload length but not the allocation capacity, it cannot safely pad that buffer in place. I kept the helper for direct unit coverage, but a665d46c4 leaves the local array uninitialized and only copies plus zero-fills when padding is actually needed, so the common path does no extra clearing.

Re [the duplicate `to_client()` guard](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcp-relay/pull/133#issuecomment-5507473966): addressed in a665d46c4. I removed this guard; the production callback performs the length validation before dispatch.

Re [the `send_udp()` Doxygen signature](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcp-relay/pull/133#issuecomment-5507619796): addressed in a665d46c4. The header documentation now uses `in_addr src_ip`, includes `pad`, and documents all parameters consistently. I also removed the stale duplicate block from the implementation.

@ashutosh-agrawal @yxieca — could you please help review this DHCP-related PR? It is non-draft, CI is green, and it adds F2 physical-member DHCPv6 relay support.

@Xichen96 Quick note on naming — "interface" means different things in dhcp6relay, and it's easy to mix them up.

In update_vlan_mapping(), interface is the VLAN member port from VLAN_MEMBER|Vlan1000|<member> (e.g. Ethernet19, PortChannel1001). That's not VLAN_INTERFACE — that table is only used earlier to check the VLAN has an IPv6 address.

For reference:

- relay_config.interface = the VLAN (Vlan1000)
- interface here = member port from VLAN_MEMBER
- intf in client_callback() = kernel ifname on the packet (often a physical Ethernet* even when the VLAN member is a PortChannel)

The PR makes sense — packets hit physical LAG members but vlan_map only has the PortChannel, so portchannel_map bridges the gap. Minor nit: renaming interface to member_port or vlan_member would help.
@ashutosh-agrawal Renamed the local variable to `vlan_member` to distinguish the `VLAN_MEMBER` entry from the relay VLAN interface.
